column1: # dt/unmatched-allow.tsv -- every `compatible` in dt/*.dts that no schema in
# the corpus tools/dtcheck.py runs against describes, with the reason.
# 量 2026-09-09, and it is the reason this file exists: `dt-validate` is SILENT
# on a node whose compatible matches no schema unless it is given `-m`, and it
# exits 0 either way.  So the default reading of a green is "every node was
# checked", and the truth is "every node that happened to have a schema was
# checked".  dtcheck.py passes -m and turns an undeclared unmatched compatible
# into a finding, which makes this file the enumeration of what is NOT checked.
# A row here is a scope limit, never an excuse.  Adding one is a decision that
# a node is described elsewhere or not yet described at all; deleting one is
# what happens when a binding arrives.
# 🔴 2026-09-20 (eighty-ninth segment): FIVE OF THE SEVEN ROWS BELOW SAY
# "Validated when --extra-schema points at a kernel tree", AND THAT HATCH
# DOES NOT OPEN.  量, same .dtb, same schemas, only the packaging changed:
# one `-s` gives 4 unmatched and two give 11, because a second `-s` makes
# this project's own six bindings stop matching.  It is version-INDEPENDENT
# -- equally broken under the dtschema 2026.6 that ci.yml now pins -- and it
# was never caught because CI never passes the flag.
# So those five rows presently name a remedy nobody can run.  They stay,
# because the scope limit they declare is TRUE and deleting them would hide
# it; what is false is the sentence about how to lift it.
# ⚠️ AND A SECOND THING THIS FILE COULD NOT SAY UNTIL NOW.  An unmatched
# compatible does not only leave its node's BINDING unchecked -- it leaves
# that node's PROPERTIES untyped, and an untyped property is not validated
# at all.  量 2026-09-20 with a negative control in the same command: supply
# minimal `gpio-keys` and `gpio-leds` schemas and dtschema 2026.9 reports 0
# complaints about `linux,code`, `debounce-interval` and `default-state`;
# omit them and it reports 3.  dtcheck's `C2` enumerates unmatched
# COMPATIBLES and cannot see the property half, which is why 2026.9 going
# red looked like a regression and was a stricter instrument reporting a
# scope limit that was always there.  docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md carries what
# would settle both.
# compatible<TAB>reason
gpio-leds
column2: kernel subsystem binding (Documentation/devicetree/bindings/leds/leds-gpio.yaml); not in dtschema's corpus. Validated when --extra-schema points at a kernel tree.

realtek,rtl8196e-nor
column2: 🔴 NOT described anywhere yet. The NOR device behind the controller has no binding of its own in this project, because nothing has read a JEDEC id from it -- SPEC.md F3 has that as an open item and R5-5's driver reaches the chip through an UNKNOWN-chip fallback. A binding written before the id is read would name a part nobody has identified.

column1: lexra,rlx4181
column2: 🔴 The cpu node.  Two reasons it has no binding here and both are worth reading: `lexra` is NOT a registered device-tree vendor prefix, and this compatible string is the ONE contact docs/blind-write-ledger.md § 4.6 records with a third-party port (shibajee's rtl8196e.dtsi, fetched 2026-08-25 for CPU-25).  Writing a binding for it would turn a recorded, dated contact into an artefact of this project.  The VALUE is independently 量 on this die -- PRId 0x0000CD01 -> PRID_IMP_RLX4181.
